newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pakhoed sees double-digit growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Pakhoed sees double-digit growth in '97.

text.p: Dutch tank storage and shipping company Koninklijke Pakhoed NV said on Tuesday it expected to see double-digit growth in profit this year.

"We expect to see a significantly higher result (from ordinary operations) than the 138 million (guilders) of this year.... That means double-digit growth," Pakhoed chairman Klaas Westdijk told a news conference after the release of the company's figures.
He added the increase would be after the payout to holders of preference shares which is likely to amount to 12 million guilders this year.
The rise would come because of a combination of four factors, Pakhoed said.
The contribution of distribution activities will increase. Last year's full acquisition of Univar meant the sector accounted for 44 percent of all Pakhoed's activities.
This year, Univar in North America intends to increase its gross margin by half a percent.
"This may not sound that much, but it is equivalent to 65 million guilders," said Westdijk.
In oil storage, Pakhoed's activities in Rotterdam, which were loss-making in 1996, are expected to return to profits this year.
In shipping, its chemical shipping contract position also suggested growth, Pakhoed said.
Finally, Pakhoed should benefit from a stronger dollar.
"For every 10 guilder cent rise of the dollar, our profit rises by 4.5 million guilders," Westdijk said.
